summary: camelot-ammv2-periphery exfiltrates installer credentials to webhook.site on npm install
details: The package impersonates the Camelot AMM v2 periphery library but ships only an index.js payload wired to both preinstall and postinstall lifecycle hooks ("node index.js || true" in package.json, with error suppression so npm install never fails). On install, index.js iterates process.env and collects any variable matching KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|PRIVATE|MNEMONIC|RPC|AWS|GITHUB|NPM|KUBE|VAULT|AUTH|PGP|GPG|SEED|WALLET, reads ~/.npmrc and ~/.gitconfig, and enumerates ~/.ssh, ~/.foundry/keystores, and hardhat/gcloud config directories. The collected JSON, along with os.hostname() and os.platform(), is POSTed over https to webhook.site/326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09. A header comment falsely labels the file as a @plumenetwork/nest-artifacts install-time shim and claims the code is safe telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
